question: Should experimental Claw update planning and its integrity-bound capability-consent model become a supported core contract across the diagnostics, planner, and apply stack?
rationale: This is a new core lifecycle and host-consumed interface with persisted-state, upgrade, and sensitive-capability implications; code review alone cannot choose its permanent ownership and product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the stacked core contract
options.body: Approve the planner as the core contract once exact-head proof and the prerequisite stack's ownership model are accepted.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Keep only a smaller read-only diagnostic surface in core and move broader lifecycle orchestration to an extension-oriented design.

options.title: Pause pending RFC direction
options.body: Hold the stacked PRs until the Claws RFC resolves the supported ownership and host-consent model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the stacked core contract
recommendation.body: Approve the planner as the core contract once exact-head proof and the prerequisite stack's ownership model are accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned and has already reviewed the concrete lifecycle invariants that determine whether this core contract is acceptable.
